\section[finora]{finora — so far, until now}

\label{lesson:IT-C280-finora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for early, then the Italian for the stage.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: finora}
\textbf{finora} — \textquotedblleft{}so far, until now\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Finora è andato tutto bene.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{So far everything has gone well.}
\end{quote}

Also written \emph{fino ad ora}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{finora} fuses \emph{fino} \textquotedblleft{}up to\textquotedblright{}, built on Latin \emph{fīnis} \textquotedblleft{}end, limit\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{ora} \textquotedblleft{}now\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{hōra} \textquotedblleft{}hour\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{finora}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{finora}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{finora}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for early, then the Italian for the stage, then say \emph{finora} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does finora mean? (\textquotedblleft{}So far, until now\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[da allora]{da allora — since then, ever since}

\label{lesson:IT-C280-da-allora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the stage, then the Italian for so far.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: da allora}
\textbf{da allora} — \textquotedblleft{}since then, ever since\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ci siamo conosciuti a scuola e da allora siamo amici.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We met at school and we have been friends ever since.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Da allora in poi} — from then on.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{allora} is inherited from Latin \emph{ad illam hōram} \textquotedblleft{}at that hour\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB); \emph{da} \textquotedblleft{}from\textquotedblright{} is usually traced to Latin \emph{dē ab}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{da allora}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{da allora}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{da allora}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the stage, then the Italian for so far, then say \emph{da allora} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does da allora mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Since then, ever since\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[tuttora]{tuttora — still, to this day}

\label{lesson:IT-C280-tuttora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for so far, then the Italian for since then.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: tuttora}
\textbf{tuttora} — \textquotedblleft{}still, to this day\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Mio nonno abita tuttora nella stessa casa.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My grandfather still lives in the same house.}
\end{quote}

Stronger than \emph{ancora}: true then and true now.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tuttora} fuses \emph{tutta} \textquotedblleft{}all\textquotedblright{} and \emph{ora} \textquotedblleft{}hour, now\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{hōra} (EtymDB): all the hours up to now.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tuttora}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tuttora}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{tuttora}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for so far, then the Italian for since then, then say \emph{tuttora} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does tuttora mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Still, to this day\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[ultimamente]{ultimamente — lately}

\label{lesson:IT-C280-ultimamente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for since then, then the Italian for still.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: ultimamente}
\textbf{ultimamente} — \textquotedblleft{}lately\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ultimamente dormo poco.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Lately I have not been sleeping much.}
\end{quote}

With the present or the \emph{passato prossimo}: \emph{ultimamente ho lavorato molto}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ultimamente} is built on \emph{ultimo} \textquotedblleft{}last\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{ultimus} \textquotedblleft{}farthest, last\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ultimamente}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ultimamente}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{ultimamente}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for since then, then the Italian for still, then say \emph{ultimamente} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does ultimamente mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Lately\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[precedentemente]{precedentemente — previously, beforehand}

\label{lesson:IT-C280-precedentemente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for still, then the Italian for lately.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: precedentemente}
\textbf{precedentemente} — \textquotedblleft{}previously, beforehand\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Come ho detto precedentemente, il negozio è chiuso.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{As I said previously, the shop is closed.}
\end{quote}

Formal; in speech, \emph{prima}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{precedentemente} is built on \emph{precedente} \textquotedblleft{}previous\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{praecēdēns}, the present participle of \emph{praecēdere} \textquotedblleft{}to go before\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{precedentemente}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{precedentemente}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{precedentemente}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for still, then the Italian for lately, then say \emph{precedentemente} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[(dialogue)]{Ripasso: quando e come}

\label{lesson:IT-R280-ripasso-273-280}



\begin{quote}
Say the Italian for at first and first of all.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item at first, first of all, later on, subsequently, after which
  \item in the meantime, at the same time, as soon as, at a certain point, all of a sudden
  \item to happen, to happen to someone, to occur, to take place, what happened
  \item the event, the affair, the matter, the chronology, the sequence
  \item to last, the length of time, the instant, the moment, the phase
  \item the beginning, to finish, to conclude, the conclusion, to resume
  \item the interruption, to suspend, to put off, early, the stage
  \item so far, since then, still, lately, previously
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
At first? (\textbf{dapprima}.) First of all? (\textbf{innanzitutto}.) Later on? (\textbf{in seguito}.) Subsequently? (\textbf{successivamente}.) After which? (\textbf{dopodiché}.) In the meantime? (\textbf{nel frattempo}.) At the same time? (\textbf{contemporaneamente}.) As soon as? (\textbf{non appena}.) At a certain point? (\textbf{a un certo punto}.) All of a sudden? (\textbf{d'un tratto}.) To happen? (\textbf{accadere}.) To happen to someone? (\textbf{capitare}.) To occur? (\textbf{verificarsi}.) To take place? (\textbf{avvenire}.) What happened? (\textbf{l'accaduto}.) The event? (\textbf{l'avvenimento}.) The affair? (\textbf{la vicenda}.) The matter? (\textbf{la faccenda}.) The chronology? (\textbf{la cronologia}.) The sequence? (\textbf{la sequenza}.) To last? (\textbf{durare}.) The length of time? (\textbf{la durata}.) The instant? (\textbf{l'istante}.) The moment? (\textbf{l'attimo}.) The phase? (\textbf{la fase}.) The beginning? (\textbf{il principio}.) To finish? (\textbf{terminare}.) To conclude? (\textbf{concludere}.) The conclusion? (\textbf{la conclusione}.) To resume? (\textbf{riprendere}.) The interruption? (\textbf{l'interruzione}.) To suspend? (\textbf{sospendere}.) To put off? (\textbf{rimandare}.) Early? (\textbf{in anticipo}.) The stage? (\textbf{la tappa}.) So far? (\textbf{finora}.) Since then? (\textbf{da allora}.) Still? (\textbf{tuttora}.) Lately? (\textbf{ultimamente}.) Previously? (\textbf{precedentemente}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
